title: Ingress lane contracts
description: Semantics of externally-writable spans of the universal vector: what each position means, in what unit, over what value domain, convertible how. Deliberately separate from region-allocation.schema.json, which stays the authority on allocation — which span belongs to whom. Generated by scripts/backfill-lane-contracts.py and consumed by the lane projector, which resolves each axis as its lane profile overlaid with the axis's own overrides.

ucumCode.description: A UCUM code in canonical form. Canonicality is not expressible in JSON Schema and is enforced by scripts/ucum.py in the generator and in tests/contracts/lane_contracts_test.py: the guardrail shapes compare codes as strings, so 'mg/dL' and 'mg.dL-1' must not both occur.

conversionPolicy.description: prohibited is required for ordinal and nominal scales: rescaling a category is a category error, not an arithmetic one.

unitContract.description: The unit half of an axis. Appears on a derivation profile and, as an override, on an individual axis.

contendedNames.description: Alternative names other writers give this position, kept so the arbiter sees the divergence when it resolves the cell.

derivationProfiles.description: Named unit contracts a lane can adopt wholesale, keyed '<normalization>/<bitsPerElement>'. Factoring these out keeps a rule change one edit rather than thousands, and keeps the rule legible.

id.description: Matches the pattern reg:IngressLaneShape enforces, so a lane id that projects cleanly here cannot be refused there.

readers.description: Machines reading this lane. Several machines legitimately share one externally-written region, which is why a lane is a region rather than a machine.

axes.description: Empty when the lane is unresolved; the reason is then in review. An axis carries what varies — position and meaning — plus any override of its lane's profile.

contention.description: Cells of this lane whose next value is contended by more than one writer, read from domains/arbitration-registry.json, which is the authority on both contention and its resolution. Contention is the normal state of an ingress lane, not a defect.

contendedCells.description: The contended cells themselves, not a count, so the sidecar stays checkable against the registry.

machineWriters.description: Machines whose output region writes cells of this lane. M1(output i) feeding M2(input j) is the interconnect mechanism, so an ingress lane is normally written from inside as well as outside — 703 of 983 lanes have at least one.

permittedProviders.description: External writer classes admitted into this lane. Machine outputs write the same cells and are listed separately in machineWriters.

carriesAutonomy.description: The autonomy a value admitted here carries FORWARD. Autonomy is transitive: it rides the value through the arbiter into the next machine's input, the minimum along a chain dominates, and acting above it takes a specific approval.

requiredAutonomy.description: Autonomy floor a writer must hold. Required on life-safety lanes.

semanticContention.description: Writers contending for this lane do not agree on what its cells mean. Flagged rather than eliminated: the divergence is surfaced through the arbiter as a second check on the semantic integrity of the deterministic core.

enforcement.description: How a runtime treats a violation here. Staged per lane because 991 lanes cannot go to blocking on one day, and staged in the corpus rather than per-runtime config so four runtimes cannot drift.

labelInconsistent.description: The machine's normalization label is contradicted by its element width. The positions are read from the width and the values; the corpus review decides which side to correct.

semanticsDerivedFrom.description: The machine whose input region covers this service lane and whose inputSemantics named its positions.

alsoDeclaredAs.description: Other ids under which this same region is declared. One region, one contract.

review.description: Lanes the evidence does not settle. These are not defects in the generator: a fabricated unit behind a guardrail is worse than an absent one, so anything unresolved is surfaced rather than guessed.
